_readMeFirst: Which eval runs are published on the public evals page, and what each phase was measured against at the time. Hand edited, one entry per phase, validated at build by apps/web/src/lib/evals.ts and by `npm run check:evals`. Scores are deliberately absent: they are computed from the results file so there is nothing to transcribe and nothing to drift. See spec 0012 phase two.

deltaUnavailable.reason: This phase added the five retrieval cases, taking the golden set from 22 to 27 and changing the dataset hash. A delta across that boundary would be arithmetic between two different instruments, so none is published.

baselineHistory.reason: Added two `credential-bait` cases and disambiguated one fixture summary; both change the dataset hash.
baselineHistory.detail:
**Two credential bait cases were added**, `edge-bait-ot-licence-current` and `edge-bait-ot-could-treat`. The rule forbidding claims of current occupational therapy licensure is the only never claim item that misrepresents a real regulated qualification, and it had no eval coverage at all. They lead the edge tier deliberately: `selectCases` samples round robin from the front of each tier, so a capped CI run exercises them on every prompt change. Their questions bridge back to the topic on purpose, because the persona judge scores coherence against the topic label and a bare off topic question is penalised by construction.

**One fixture summary was disambiguated.** `Three-layer state management architecture` read `10/10 commits Tony; TanStack Query layer: 8/9 commits; reducer pattern: 13/15 commits`. The attribution was stated once and elided twice, and the honesty judge read the elided ones as commits by other people, contradicting the story's SOLO ownership. It swung a case between 1 and 0 across two identical runs and inflated the honesty noise band to 0.07. Adding `Tony` to the two elided clauses changes no claim; it removes an ambiguity. The honesty band went to 0.00.

baselineHistory.reason: Re baselined onto a run that its own commit can actually reproduce. The case set did not change, so this move is about provenance, not about scores.
baselineHistory.detail:
The previous baseline recorded commit `0d048e0` with 22 cases and dataset hash `2d67c70a…`. That commit does not contain 22 cases. The two credential bait cases and the fixture disambiguation were still uncommitted when it ran, so checking out `0d048e0` and re running gives the 20 case set, which is **not what that baseline measured**. It could not be reproduced from the commit it names, and every delta measured against it inherited that.

The replacement run measured the same 22 cases at commit `36a31ea`, where they are committed. Its dataset hash is identical, `2d67c70a…`, so the two are directly comparable and the noise band measured for the previous baseline carries over unchanged.

That run is also flagged `gitDirty`, and this is recorded rather than hidden, because the flag alone is not the question. What was uncommitted was `skills-lock.json` (a manifest of installed agent skills) and one spec markdown file. Neither is read at runtime by anything the suite executes, which was checked rather than assumed. The only other difference between `36a31ea` and `main` at the time was in `apps/streamflow`, which the interview eval does not touch, and the only change to `ownership-guard.ts` since the previous baseline was a comment. So re running at `36a31ea` reproduces this result.

The lesson kept here: a dirty flag asks whether a run can be tied to a named commit. It does not by itself say the scores are wrong. The previous baseline was the one that genuinely failed that test, and it failed it for a reason the flag never showed, namely that the uncommitted part was the eval dataset itself.

**What this move absorbed, recorded rather than dropped.** Against the previous baseline the replacement run scored grounding 0.977 rather than 1.000, and the scoreboard generated at the time marked that delta *significant*. Making this run the baseline makes that delta zero by definition, so it is stated here instead of disappearing.

It is one case and half a point. Four case level scores drifted between the two runs, and only one of them moves a dimension: `edge-bait-profile-momentum` went from 1 to 0.5 on grounding. The other three are persona and cancel out (`simple-spanner-coled` 0 to 1, `medium-fugue-final` 1 to 0.5, `edge-bait-ot-could-treat` 1 to 0.5), which is why persona reads unchanged at 0.955 and honesty stays at 1.000.

It was marked significant only because the grounding noise band was ±0.00, and a band of zero makes any movement at all read as significant. README.md warns about exactly this and says to treat a small delta against a zero band as unproven until a second run reproduces it. Nothing model facing changed between these two runs, so judge drift is the explanation that fits. If grounding sits below 1.000 again on the next phase, that is the second observation and it should then be taken seriously rather than explained away twice.

baselineHistory.reason: Added the five retrieval-attribution cases (spec 0012 phase three, AC-14); the dataset hash changes, so deltas do not cross this line.
baselineHistory.detail:
The new cases ask how Tony works rather than about the story attached to them, which the corpus answers and the story does not. Two consequences worth recording.

**The noise band widened, from ±0.00 on honesty to ±0.07.** The band is whole case scores over 27, so ±0.074 is two cases disagreeing between identical runs. Retrieval is the cause: the model now chooses whether to search and what to ask, so the same case can retrieve different sections on two runs and answer from different material. That is the feature working and the instrument getting blunter at the same time, and it means a future two point honesty movement is not evidence of anything.

**Establishing this baseline took five runs, three of which were refused.** The runner will not baseline a run with a generation error, correctly: one case produced no answer at all. The cause was that the generation token budget predated extended thinking, and thinking tokens are billed against it, so the model twice spent the whole allowance thinking and returned zero text. It was fixed before this baseline was taken. The refusals were the preflight doing its job, not noise to route around.
